query_architecture.description: v0.19 defines the internal QueryPlan structure and execution strand model [Decision 4].

query_node_tree.linear_pipeline: MATCH -> WHERE -> WITH -> GROUP BY -> HAVING -> ORDER BY -> LIMIT/SKIP -> RETURN. Clauses hold optional references to the next node in the strand.
query_node_tree.branch_points: UNION holds child pipelines. Subqueries (EXISTS, IN) embed child QueryPlans.

node_variants.fields: start_var, end_var, edge_type, weight_field, weight_algo, var_name, next?

node_variants.desc: Filters grouped rows. Structurally valid only as a successor to GroupByNode. Aggregation expressions are evaluated against the grouped result set at this stage.

node_variants.fields: left: QueryPlan, right: QueryPlan, all: bool

view_eligibility: View defined over compatible predicate (same field access pattern).
View covers at least the fields referenced in predicate and RETURN projections.
cross_type_node_strategy.fallback: Full cross-partition scan if no eligible view exists. Emits WARN-PERF-004 if unindexed.

return_expr_variants.desc: A struct literal whose values are themselves struct literals. Example: RETURN { location: { city: p.city, zip: p.zip } }

order_expr.defaults: NULLS LAST for ASC, NULLS FIRST for DESC.

parameter_binding.description: v0.19 uses plan-time inference [Decision 6]. Parameters are storable parts of a QueryPlan.
resolution_rules: Inferred from schema context (e.g. p.age > $min_age where p is Person).
Ambiguous contexts require explicit annotation: $param: Type.
Ambiguity without annotation is hard error [2026] Parameter Type Ambiguous.
Value type checking against resolved type occurs at run-time [2025].

fat_arrow.meaning: Binds node to role (CREATE/MERGE) or filters by existing binding (MATCH)

arrow_operator_summary.design_rationale: Visual distinction between schema (<- ->) and instance (=>) prevents ambiguity.

write_clauses.syntax: CREATE NODE variable:TypeName { key = value, ... }; | CREATE NODE [ ...batch... ];
write_clauses.description: Creates new node entities. Node-level constraints and default values are evaluated before creation. v0.19: Rejects abstract type handles with [4010].

batch_syntax.description: Atomic creation of multiple nodes. Implicitly wrapped in a transaction.

write_clauses.validation: Evaluates all node constraints. Fails with [3011] if any constraint is violated. Enforces [3015] if a required field with no default is omitted.
write_clauses.example: CREATE NODE alice:Person { id = UUID(), name = "Alice", age = 25 };

write_clauses.syntax: CREATE EDGE variable:TypeName { field = value, role => node, ... }; | CREATE EDGE [ ...batch... ];
write_clauses.description: Creates new hyperedges. Role binding uses '=>' to assign specific nodes to roles. Validates cardinality, role constraints, and edge constraints before creation. v0.19: Rejects abstract edge handles with [4011].

batch_syntax.syntax: CREATE EDGE [ e1:Type { role => n1 }, e2:Type { role => n2 } ];

binding_operator.purpose: Binds a node instance to a role

validation.order: 1. Validate nodes exist, 2. Validate cardinality bounds, 3. Validate role constraints, 4. Validate edge constraints
validation.error_codes: [3014] for cardinality, [3012] for role, [3013] for edge

write_clauses.example: CREATE EDGE m:Marriage { husband => doug, wife => nini, date = DATE("1999/08/20") };

write_clauses.description: Cross-type atomic creation with shared variable scope. Variables bound in the NODE sub-block are in scope for the EDGE sub-block within the same statement.
write_clauses.atomicity: The entire statement is atomic (all-or-nothing). Error in any entry rolls back the entire batch.
write_clauses.example: CREATE [ NODE [ lucy:Person { ... }, nova:Dog { ... } ], EDGE [ dmn:Owns { owner => lucy, pet => nova } ] ];

write_clauses.syntax: MERGE (var: TypeName { role => node, ... }) [ON CREATE SET ...] [ON MATCH SET ...]
write_clauses.description: Upsert operation. Supports Property-Based Matching OR Role-Binding Matching (if @unique constraint exists on roles).
write_clauses.v019_semantics: DEFAULT values apply ONLY on the ON CREATE path. Null in pattern acts as wildcard.

computed_fields.behavior: @computed fields cannot be set via MERGE [2040]

write_clauses.description: Soft property merge update from a parameter map.
Bulk property update. Merges provided properties into node/edge, preserving unmentioned fields.
write_clauses.example: MATCH (p:Person { id = $id }) SET p += { active = true, last_updated = NOW() };

write_clauses.syntax: SET variable.role += node | SET variable.role += [node1, node2]
write_clauses.description: Atomic Append. Adds node(s) to a role collection. Enforces cardinality [3014].
Atomic Remove. Removes node(s) from a role collection. Enforces cardinality [3014].

write_clauses.syntax: SET variable.field = value | SET variable.role = [n1, n2]
write_clauses.description: Updates specific properties or fully replaces a role collection.
Deletes a node or edge. Fails if connected [4001].

read_clauses.syntax: IMPORT Name.Space; | IMPORT SCHEMA Name FROM Name.Space; | IMPORT "Path" AS Alias
read_clauses.description: Imports namespaces or named schema units.
Matches nodes and edges. v0.19: MATCH on abstract type matches all concrete subtypes.

syntax_enforcement.note: ':' for filters, '=' for assignments. Mixing is Syntax Error [1001].

read_clauses.syntax: MATCH PATH var = (start)-[:Edge* {role} WEIGHT BY field USING algo]->(end)

read_clauses.description: Filters matched results. Block syntax implies AND.
True if subquery produces any rows.
True if expression matches any subquery result.

read_clauses.syntax: field IS NULL | field IS NOT NULL

read_clauses.description: Pipeline barrier. Variables not listed are dropped from scope.

Filters grouped rows after GROUP BY aggregation. Valid only when a GROUP BY clause is present. Conditions may reference aggregation expressions and GROUP BY keys. Block syntax implies AND. Bare field references that are neither aggregated nor grouped are forbidden [1001].
read_clauses.example: MATCH (p:Person) RETURN [ p.Department, AVG(p.Salary) AS avg_sal ] GROUP BY p.Department HAVING AVG(p.Salary) > 50000;

read_clauses.description: Combines results. Branches must have equal column counts [2001]. Mismatched aliases produce [WARN-SCHEMA-004] and use left branch alias. Column types must unify: Int/Float -> Float, T/T? -> T?, common abstract parent -> Parent. All others fail with [2001].
Final projection. Supports aliasing, object literals, and tuple projections.

query_parameters.description: HyperQL supports parameterized queries for security, performance, and query plan caching.

syntax.description: Parameters use $ prefix followed by identifier. Case-sensitive.

type_binding.description: Parameter types are inferred from context on first use. Subsequent uses must match the inferred type.

usage_contexts.example: CREATE EDGE m:Marriage { date: $wedding_date, husband => $h, wife => $w }

query_preparation.support: Queries with parameters can be prepared and cached.

scope_variants.session: Dropped automatically when session ends. PREPARE stmt AS ...
scope_variants.persistent: Survives session termination; stored in schema namespace. PREPARE PERSISTENT stmt AS ...

lifecycle.management: DROP PREPARE stmt; SHOW PREPARED STATEMENTS [ALL];
lifecycle.revalidation: Persistent statements follow ALTER-triggered revalidation rules. If referenced types/fields change, statement moves to 'invalid' state [2023].
lifecycle.limits: Session limit implementation-defined; MUST support 256. Exceeding limit produces [5010].

null_handling.description: v0.19: Null parameter values are allowed for nullable fields.

introspection.description: Runs the named constraint against all existing data. Non-destructive. Returns ValidateConstraintResult as defined in Part 7.
Shows query execution plan without running the query

default.output: Human-readable text format showing plan tree

introspection.example: EXPLAIN VERBOSE MATCH (p:Person) WHERE p.age > 30 RETURN p;

introspection.description: Executes query and shows actual execution statistics alongside plan

default.output: Plan with actual row counts and timing

verbose.output: Detailed execution statistics including cache hits, I/O operations

introspection.description: Returns static analysis of a constraint expression without executing it.
Executes the constraint against all existing data and returns runtime statistics.

constraint_limits.description: Operational limits to prevent abuse and ensure stability.

udf_limits.description: Interpreter safety limits to prevent infinite loops and stack overflows.

whitespace_free_readability_guarantee: All v0.19 block syntax forms are unambiguous even if all whitespace is removed, enabled by balanced delimiters ([, ] and {, }).
